name: pOOBs4 / exFAThax - exFAT up-case table size truncation (CVE-2022-3349)

root_cause.summary: UVFAT_readupcasetable() parses the up-case table directory entry of an exFAT volume and reads dataLength as a 64-bit on-disk value. It computes the table size in 64-bit arithmetic as (sector_size + dataLength - 1) rounded down to a sector multiple, then passes that size to sceFatfsCreateHeapVl(), whose size argument is a 32-bit int. When dataLength is larger than 4 GiB the low 32 bits of the rounded size survive (for example 0x100000200 becomes 0x200), so the kernel allocates a small buffer and then reads the up-case table sector by sector into it until dataLength is satisfied, producing a linear heap overflow of attacker-controlled table data in multiples of the sector size.
root_cause.primitive: linear heap buffer overflow (out-of-bounds write) of attacker-controlled file content, length a multiple of the sector size, caused by a 64-bit to 32-bit truncation at an allocator boundary
root_cause.trigger: inserting a USB mass-storage device that holds a crafted exFAT image (the public exploit waits for the system's 'disk format not supported' notification after insertion), which makes the kernel exFAT handler parse the volume's up-case table; no further user action beyond insertion and the resulting mount attempt
root_cause.consequence: kernel heap corruption of the allocations adjacent to the undersized up-case buffer; with heap shaping this yields control of an adjacent object and kernel code execution (the public exploit reaches kernel ROP and kernel patching)

discovery_approach.summary: Two public paths converged on the same function. TheFloW found the truncation while auditing Sony's exFAT implementation and reported it to PlayStation on 2021-09-15 (HackerOne #1340942, disclosed 2022-09-21, CVE-2022-3349). Separately, after 9.03 shipped, zecoxao diffed the 9.00 and 9.03 kernels and advised the scene to exploit the vulnerability; ChendoChap, Znullptr and Specter released pOOBs4 for 9.00 on 2021-12-13. The pOOBs4 README describes its own route as a 9.00-versus-9.03 kernel diff, so the public exploit was version-diff driven even though the same defect had already been reported privately.
signals: a 64-bit length field read from disk reaches a callee whose prototype declares a 32-bit int size parameter (implicit narrowing at the call boundary)
allocation size computed as a sector-rounded value in 64-bit arithmetic and then truncated by the callee
copy loop that advances the destination pointer by sector size for dataLength bytes without any bound derived from the allocation
up-case table entry length trusted without an upper-bound check against the volume or partition size

differences: 9.03 adds an upper-32-bit test before the allocator call: the 9.03+ decompilation excerpt shows `if (table_len >> 0x20 == 0)` guarding sceFatfsCreateHeapVl(0, table_len & 0xffffffff), so a table length above 4 GiB is rejected instead of silently truncated

the same excerpt shows the block-size field read from fileSystem+0x104 in 1.01-9.00 but from fileSystem+0x4c in 9.03-13.50, a structure-layout change that accompanies the fix but is not itself the security check
the PS4 dev wiki records the same bug as fixed on PS5 in 4.50

patch_evidence.what: public decompiler-style excerpt of UVFAT_readupcasetable before and after 9.03 (PS4 dev wiki) showing the added `table_len >> 0x20 == 0` guard, plus the CVE-2022-3349 record naming the function and CWE-787
patch_evidence.limits: no firmware bytes, no Sony advisory text and no binary diff are stored or linked here; the before/after code is a wiki transcription, not a vendor patch

sources.supports: exploit needs a modified exFAT image; describes discovery by diffing 9.00 and 9.03 kernels; states the bug is fixed in 9.03 and predates 1.00; states it works on some PS5 firmwares but with no public exploitation strategy
root cause: 64-bit dataLength and size truncated by the 32-bit sceFatfsCreateHeapVl() argument; 512-byte-multiple overflow; heap spray target; reporter and disclosure dates

CVE-2022-3349 mapping, credit timeline (TheFloW find, zecoxao diff advice, ChendoChap implementation), pre-9.03 and 9.03+ pseudo-code with the added check, affected 1.01-9.00 and fixed 9.03 / PS5 4.50
official CVE description naming UVFAT_readupcasetable and dataLength, CWE-787 classification, publication date 2022-09-28

gaps: The PS4 dev wiki credits TheFloW with the find, while the pOOBs4 README describes independent discovery by diffing 9.00 and 9.03; both fit the same code path, but no source states the relationship between the two discoveries
PS5 exploitation is asserted by the repository README but no public PS5 trigger, writeup or exploit was fetched; the PS5 claim rests on that sentence and the wiki fix version
heap layout, spray object and offset constants used by the exploit are deliberately not reproduced here
the CVE record is VulDB-sourced rather than vendor-sourced, and no Sony security advisory text was fetched
